_about: Claude's drafts of rulers' lines, for Rich to review (D-62). Development builds show them beside rivalLines.json; release builds never do. To approve a line, move it into rivalLines.json under the same ruler and key (and edit it as you like). Patch 8's drafts were all approved and moved there on 2026-10-31 (D-67). Patch 10 stage 3 (R5, D-91): these are written as parts (F3, D-79). A key holding { open, body, close } builds its line from one body, with an opening and a close when given, picked by the day. Approve parts, not lines; docs/redesign/patch-10-lines.md shows built lines for each. Placeholders: {hex} a hex's name, {rival} a ruler's short name, {need} how many deeds a commission asks, {until} its last day, {days} a streak's days, {level} a wall level, {tag} a tag (Steel, Coin, Engine, Arcane), {week} a campaign week.

open: Ugrak has work for you, lordling.
body: Fight me {need} days before {until}. Any fight. Win or lose, it counts.
Bring your war to my march {need} days by {until}. Blood on the grass, every one.
close: Do it, and Ugrak speaks your name at the fires.

body: Stand and fight me {need} days before {until}, and I turn my bands for home.
Give me {need} days of real war by {until}. Do that, and there is no siege.
close: Hide behind your walls, and I come for them.

body: Good. Ugrak will be waiting.
Ha! Now we see what you are made of.
Busy? Fine. The Steppe can wait. A little.
No? Ugrak will find someone braver to fight.
You came to fight, as Ugrak asked. Good days. Ugrak counted every one.
You answered Ugrak's call with steel. The fires burn brighter for it.
Ugrak asked for a fight and the grass stayed quiet. Next time, lordling.
Ugrak waited for you in the field. You did not come. The field will still be there.
You put stones on {hex}. Level {level}. Walls are for people who fear the night.
More walls at {hex}? Ugrak will climb them. Or go around.
{days} days you have fought me now. Ugrak is starting to like you.
Day {days} in my field. The Steppe sings of stubborn lordlings.
Your companies fight with {tag} now. Good. Ugrak understands {tag}.
{tag} leads your armies. Finally, someone who fights properly.
Week {week}. You took {hex} from me. The first of many. Ugrak still remembers the smoke.
{hex}, week {week}. The first ground you took from the Steppe. It was a good fight.
Week {week}, at {hex}. That was a battle. Ugrak still has the scars.
Remember {hex}? Week {week}. The Steppe still sings about it.
In week {week} our pact ended, kept. Ugrak does not say this often: you keep your word.
Week {week}. A pact, kept to its end. Ugrak remembers.

open: Got a little opportunity for you.
body: Win me a hex by coin before {until}. A bribe, a courtship, a trade: any honest purchase will do.
Buy yourself some land before {until}. Bribe it, court it, trade for it. Just don't take it by force.
close: There's a little something in it for you.

open: Now, now, no need for sieges.
body: Win a hex by coin before {until}, and my lads go home. Business as usual.
Show me you still trade like a civilized lord. One hex bought or courted by {until}, and I call my lads back.
Pleasure doing business, friend!
Lovely. I'll draw up the papers.
No? Your loss, friend. Literally.
Pity. The offer was a bargain.
You bought your land, just as I asked. A lord who pays! I'm touched.
Deal done and delivered. You've got a merchant's soul, friend.
You didn't buy a thing this week, friend. The market reopens. It always does.
No sale this time. Never mind. I keep a ledger, not a grudge. Mostly.
Walls at {hex}, level {level}. Expensive things, walls. Who's your mason? I want a cut.
You're walling {hex}. Smart. Walls protect investments.
{rival} says you've fought him {days} days running. Expensive hobby, friend.
Day {days} fighting {rival}? Think of the coin you could be making instead.
Your companies carry {tag} now. A lord after my own heart.
{tag} leads your armies. Finally, a properly funded war.
{hex}, week {week}. The first property you ever took off me. I still have the receipt.
Week {week}. You took {hex}. I've been billing you for it ever since.
Week {week}, at {hex}. Costliest battle of my career. I still have the invoices.
Remember {hex}? Week {week}. My accountants still weep about it.
Week {week}: our pact, paid in full. I frame my best contracts, you know.
In week {week} you kept every line of our pact. I still tell the story to new customers.

open: A task, if you have the stone for it.
body: Raise {need} levels of wall on your land before {until}. Good stone, set true.
Build me {need} levels of wall by {until}. A border that holds is worth more than one that grows.
close: It will be written in the book.
Do this, and a dwarf will think better of you.

body: Raise {need} levels of wall by {until}, and my clans stand down.
Show me {need} levels of good stone by {until}, and there will be no siege from the mountain.
So. Then build well.
Agreed. I will be watching your masons.
As you like. It is noted.
Then the stone waits. It is patient. So am I.
You raised your walls, as asked. Good stone. It is written in the book, in black ink.
The walls are up, and they are true. A dwarf could not have asked for better. Well. Almost.
The walls I asked for did not rise. The mountain waits. It always does.
No new stone this week. It is noted, without anger. Build when you can.
You walled {hex} to level {level}. Good. Walls are a promise to the future.
Level {level} at {hex}. I would have cut the stone finer, but it will hold.
{rival} has fought you {days} days running, I hear. Loud work. Does he never build?
Day {days} of {rival}'s brawling. Stone outlasts shouting, outsider. Remember it.
Your companies march with {tag} now. Good. Machines are honest.
{tag} leads your armies. A dwarf could get used to you.
{hex}, week {week}. The first stone you took from me. It is in the book.
Week {week}. {hex}. I wrote it down that very night.
Week {week}, at {hex}. The book has three pages on that battle.
{hex}, week {week}. My clans still sing of it. In a minor key.
Week {week}: our word to each other, kept to its last day. That is worth more than gold under the mountain.
In week {week} our pact ran its full length. I keep that page near the front of the book.

open: A small experiment, my dear lord.
body: Before {until}, best one of my workings: take a hex of mine on its ebb, hold against a surge, or beat a mythic.
Show me you understand magic before {until}. An ebb seized, a surge held or a mythic slain will do.

open: Let us be civilized, my dear lord.
body: Best one of my workings before {until}, and I call my forces home. An ebb, a surge or a mythic: your choice.
Prove you can handle the unseen by {until}, and there will be no siege. I'd so much rather study you than conquer you.
Splendid. I'll prepare my notes.
Excellent. Let's see what you can do.
No? How disappointingly predictable.
Pity. I did so want the data.
You passed my little test. I've written it up. You come out of it rather well.
Done, and done properly. I'm almost impressed. Almost.
My experiment came to nothing this week. Results are results, even dull ones.
No result this time. Never mind. Science is mostly failure, beautifully recorded.
Walls at {hex}, level {level}. Stone against magic. How quaint. How sensible.
You've walled {hex} to level {level}. My surges will find it a pleasant puzzle.
{rival} tells me you've fought him {days} days in a row. Exhausting, surely. For him.
Day {days} of brawling with {rival}? Do tell me if either of you has an idea.
Your companies carry {tag} now. Finally, a lord who reads.
{tag} leads your armies. Do be careful. Magic bites the careless.
{hex}, week {week}. The first hex you took from me. I have a whole chapter on it.
Week {week}: you took {hex}. I was annoyed for nearly a decade. Well. An afternoon.
Week {week}, at {hex}. A fascinating battle. I've studied it since.
Remember {hex}, week {week}? I do. I remember everything.
Week {week}: our pact, kept to the letter. A useful data point about you.
In week {week} you kept every term of our pact. I've filed it under 'surprising'.
